title: A cloud worker wrote tracker state despite the prompt forbidding it — the boundary must be enforced, not requested
description:
Observed live, run_215b7cbff9dd405c80d738be45cccde5, tick 5jo, 2026-08-22 — the first cloud worker container in this project's history to complete real work.

It did good work: commit e0898b00 'herd: qualify agent names per repo' is a correct, substantial implementation of its tick. It then ALSO committed b999290f:

  tick 5jo: close — per-repo agent-name qualification landed
   .tick/activity/activity.jsonl | 2 ++
   .tick/issues/5jo.json         | 7 +++++--

It ran `tk close` and committed the result. The worker prompt forbids exactly this, in the second line of its Boundaries section: 'Do NOT run any `tk` command and do NOT touch the `.tick/` directory — the orchestrator owns all tick state.'

So the instruction is right and was ignored. The worker model is deepseek-v4-flash (the economy/balanced tier the factory routes containers at since ys3), and an instruction-following gap at that tier is a fact to design around, not a bug to file against the model.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE STRAY COMMIT: .tick/ is the orchestrator's serialized state. Several workers in a wave each closing their own tick produce conflicting writes to the same activity.jsonl and issue files, on branches that all merge into one integration commit. That is the exact conflict class the boundary invariant exists to prevent, and D4's one-writer rule with it.

The herdr substrate survives this because `tk herd collect` fails the branch closed with boundary-violation before it can merge. The cloud path has the same check in worker-collect, so it likely catches it too — VERIFY THAT FIRST, because if it does, this is a hardening tick rather than a hole.

THE FIX SHOULD BE MECHANICAL, not louder prose. The container is ours end to end, so the boundary can be enforced rather than requested. Options worth weighing:
- Deny `tk` in the worker container's PATH for the harness's own process (the entrypoint needs tk; the agent does not).
- A pre-commit hook in the worker's clone that refuses any staged path under .tick/.
- Have the entrypoint strip .tick/ changes before it commits and push a warning into the report.
The first is the strongest and the cheapest: an agent that cannot invoke tk cannot mutate tracker state by any route, including ones nobody predicted.

Whatever is chosen, the worker's report must SAY that a boundary violation was attempted, so it reaches a human instead of being silently cleaned.
acceptance_criteria: A cloud worker that tries to run tk or write under .tick/ cannot change tracker state, and its report says the attempt happened. Pinned by a test. Verified against a live worker on the model that actually did it.
